findings.reason: the plan must name the existing guard and state the reproduction of its failure (the incident launched attempt 7, so the guard did not fire) before proposing a replacement.
findings.text: §3 bullet 1 ("a coordinator's crew resume does not launch [beside a live attempt]; it refuses, naming the live attempt and its pids") is already implemented: `resume_plan` refuses with "still has a live process; observe or stop it before resuming" and `_launcher_refusal` at `reckon/crew/resumption.py:643` holds the same guard for the dry-run; the plan does not cite either, so it would build a second refusal rather than explain why this one failed on 2026-10-12

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend this gate, not to add a parallel one.
findings.text: §3 bullet 2 ("the sweep never resumes a run whose attempt is alive") is already implemented as `_observed_end_refusal`, which refuses a lift unless `local_liveness` + `live_worker_pid` observe the end; the plan's sweep guard duplicates it

findings.reason: §2 must establish why the existing liveness read let the run classify complete, rather than re-specifying the invariant it already asserts.
findings.text: §2 bullet 3 ("a run whose recorded worker pid is still alive is never classified complete or scoring") already has its machinery here: `local_liveness` (line 149), the worker-record read (line 154) and the descendant read `_live_descendant` (line 170), with the classifier comment "the live process outranks every worker-reported outcome"; the plan cites none of it

findings.reason: the plan should name `routing.py::signal_worker` as the owner to extend (add descendant/group reach there) so every caller of the primitive gains it, instead of forking a kill path in the dispatch module that only `terminate` reaches.
findings.text: §2 bullet 2 ("crew stop ends every live descendant of the run's recorded supervisor and worker pids, plus any process whose working directory lies in the run's worktree") puts a second kill-and-enumerate path in `terminate`, while the signalling owner is `reckon/crew/routing.py:2837 signal_worker` (its docstring: "the only function in the crew that calls os.kill or os.killpg") and the cwd-holder enumerator is `reckon/crew/routing.py:2512 _processes_holding` ("Name the processes holding path as their cwd or as an open file"); the descendant enumerator is `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:258 _process_children` / `:289 _live_descendant`

findings.reason: the fix belongs at the shared owner so all nine callers inherit it; naming only `terminate` bounds the repair to one door.
findings.text: census of the same defect: `signal_worker` is imported by nine modules (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:49`, `promotion_release.py:35`, `promotion_checks.py:44`, `recovery_watch.py:29`, `recovery_stream.py:21`, `recovery_review_delivery.py:18`, `dispatch.py:137`, `promotion.py:117`, `dispatch_sessions.py:36`); a descendant-killing added only inside `terminate` leaves every other release path (promotion, recovery, review delivery) still signalling one pid and leaving children

findings.reason: the plan must say the existing grace/SIGKILL ends the worker but not the worker's tree, so the node's scope is the descendants under the worker, not the worker-kill path itself.
findings.text: §2 bullet 1 ("the supervisor's exit path ends the worker's whole process tree before it records the exit") already escalates the direct worker to SIGKILL after `STOP_GRACE` (`dispatch_launch.py:2830`, `:2897`, `STOP_GRACE_ENV` at `:2556`), and `tests/test_a_stopped_run_ends_its_supervisor.py` locks it in; the genuinely new part is only the worker's *children* (the orphan's pytest), which the plan does not distinguish from the already-covered direct worker

findings.reason: a fourth test file asserting the same guards adds surface and re-green-scopes existing tests; the plan should extend the existing files with the pointer-lock/other-host case instead.
findings.text: §3's done-when file `tests/test_a_resume_never_launches_beside_a_live_attempt.py` restates cases already covered: `tests/test_resume_refuses_a_live_worker.py` (resume refused over a live worker, naming the pid), `tests/test_resume_sweep_needs_an_observed_death.py` (sweep refuses without an observed end) and `tests/test_direct_resume_needs_an_observed_death.py` (direct resume needs an observed death); all landed 2026-10-03

findings.reason: §2 must state which manifest state still classifies complete under a live worker, since this test already asserts the precedence holds.
findings.text: §2 bullet 3's invariant is already locked by this test ("a live process outranks every manifest-derived unreadable classification"); §2 proposes it as new

findings.reason: if the defect is the lock window (a TOCTOU between the read and the check), the extension of the existing guard is the smaller, non-forking change and the plan should say so.
findings.text: §3 says resume "checks, under the run's pointer lock, whether a supervisor or worker for the run is alive", adding a lock-scoped layer over the reading `record_process_alive` already performs, without saying why `resume_plan`'s existing guard (read pointer at `:1018`, check at `:1021`) cannot simply be moved inside the pointer lock

findings.reason: a single query returning the run's live process set (supervisor, worker, descendants, cwd-holders) behind one interface would let terminate, the supervisor exit and the classifier all consume it; the plan's three-way spread leaves each caller to recompose the set and drift.
findings.text: §2 spreads one behaviour, "end the run's live process set and report what was ended", across `dispatch_launch.py` (supervisor exit), `dispatch_sessions.py` (terminate) and `recovery_classification.py` (classification), while the reads and signals it needs live in `reckon/crew/process_liveness.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py` and `reckon/crew/routing.py` — three write paths, no owner

findings.reason: §3's text must account for the added refusal wording and the new advice state — either naming the existing refusal it supersedes or stating why the state cannot fold into the existing attempt/advice fields.
findings.text: the section adds a new refusal (resume refusing a live attempt) and a new retained state ("pending advice" in the run directory, no such machinery exists in `reckon/crew/`) without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be; public_definitions 1682, cli_options 349, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23

findings.reason: the section must state what new public definition (or none) the census adds, since the readers it needs already exist and only their consumers change.
findings.text: §2 adds descendant/child enumeration and a "reports any process still alive afterwards" outcome to `crew stop`, extending the refusal/report surface of the CLI, without naming what it retires or merging it into the existing `_processes_holding`/`_live_descendant` readers; public_definitions 1682, cli_options 349, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §2's single behaviour (end a run's live process set) is spread across three write-path modules while the machinery it needs lives in two others, so no module hides the behaviour behind a smaller interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2's `dispatch_sessions.py::terminate` change re-implements process signalling and process enumeration that `reckon/crew/routing.py` and `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py` already own.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1682, cli_options 349, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23; §3 adds a refusal and a new retained "pending advice" state without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 and §3 each propose guards and process-tree machinery that already exist in `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py`, `reckon/crew/resumption.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py` and `reckon/crew/routing.py`, and neither section cites any of them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 adds a new refusal path beside the existing `resume_plan`/`_observed_end_refusal` guards without saying why the existing guard cannot be extended under the pointer lock.
